prd.name: Saved Connections
prd.overview: A list of saved SSH hosts on the home screen so the user can tap a row to connect in one step, instead of retyping host, port, username, and credentials every session. Connections are stored locally on the device; the same hardware is the only place the secrets ever live.

requirement.name: Saved Connections List
requirement.description: After onboarding, the app's home is a list of saved SSH connections rather than an empty Connection form. Each row represents one saved host and is the user's single tap into a session.
requirement.rule: After onboarding completes, the first screen the user lands on is the saved-connections list, not the Connection form.
When the list has no entries, the screen shows a friendly empty state with a single primary "Add Connection" action.
Each row's primary line shows the user-chosen label for the entry. When the user has not chosen a label, the primary line defaults to "username@host".
Each row's secondary line shows "username@host:port". The port is omitted from the secondary line when it equals the SSH default of 22.
Each row shows a small badge indicating its authentication method (password vs. private key) so the user can tell them apart at a glance.
A "+" button in the screen's top-trailing toolbar opens the New Connection form.
The list preserves the order in which entries were added (newest at the bottom) across launches. v1 does not auto-sort by recency or usage.

requirement.name: Tap to Connect
requirement.description: Tapping a saved row connects to that host using the existing prewarm + SSH path. The user never sees the form fields again unless they explicitly edit or add an entry.
requirement.rule: Tapping a saved row immediately starts the connection flow for that entry's credential — no intermediate form.
While a connection attempt is in flight, the tapped row shows an inline progress indicator and is not tappable again until the attempt resolves.

A failed connection surfaces its error inline beneath the row that triggered it, with the same wording the Connection screen uses today (including the LAN permission "Open Settings / Retry" affordances when applicable).
The LAN local-network prewarm flow (MVP R7) is reused unchanged — the saved entry's host is fed into the same prewarm check before the SSH handshake.
Host-key mismatch handling (MVP R6) is reused unchanged — a mismatch pushes the existing mismatch screen onto the navigation stack; trusting the new key auto-retries the connect.
A successful connection transitions the user to the terminal session the same way the Connection form does today.

requirement.name: Add and Edit a Connection
requirement.description: Adding a new entry and editing an existing one share the same form. Saving is the only outcome of the form in v1 — connecting happens by returning to the list and tapping the row.
requirement.rule: The "+" action opens the form with empty fields, port pre-filled to 22, auth method defaulting to Password.
A swipe action or context-menu "Edit" on a row opens the same form pre-filled with that entry's host, port, username, label, and auth method.

The form exposes an optional "Label" text field. When the user leaves it blank, the entry is saved with an empty label and the row renders "username@host" as its primary line per R1.row_primary_label.

The form's primary action is "Save". On Save, validation matches the Connection form today (host, port, username required; port numeric; private-key file imported when key auth is selected). On success the form is dismissed and the new or updated entry appears in the list.
The form has no "Connect" button in v1. Saving is the only outcome; the user connects by tapping the saved row.

In edit mode, the password / passphrase / private-key fields are rendered as masked or "Stored — replace?" placeholders. Leaving them untouched preserves the existing secret; entering new content overwrites it.
A "Cancel" action discards any unsaved changes and returns to the list without modifying the entry.

requirement.name: Delete a Connection
requirement.description: The user can remove a saved entry. Deletion is destructive but recoverable only by re-entering the credentials manually, so it requires an explicit confirmation.
requirement.rule: A trailing swipe action on a row exposes "Delete".
A long-press context menu on a row also exposes "Delete" (alongside "Edit") for users who prefer that gesture.
Tapping Delete shows a confirmation prompt ("Delete \"<label>\"? This will remove the saved password / key.") with Cancel and a destructive Delete.
Confirming Delete removes both the index entry and the underlying Keychain item that holds the secret — no orphaned secret remains.
After confirmation, the row animates out of the list using the standard system list-row removal animation.

requirement.name: Local-Only Storage
requirement.description: Saved connections — including passwords, private keys, and passphrases — never leave the device. iCloud Keychain sync, backup-based restore, and any cross-device sharing are explicitly out of scope for v1.
requirement.rule: Each saved entry's secret material (password, private key, passphrase) is stored in the iOS Keychain with this-device-only accessibility, matching the protection class already used by the MVP credentials store.
No saved-connection material is written to iCloud, iCloud Keychain, or any other off-device store. Restoring the app on a new device starts with an empty list.

When the device is locked, the saved entries cannot be read — the app surfaces an inline "Couldn't load saved connections — device locked. Retry." banner if launched into this state and recovers when the user unlocks.

requirement.name: Migration from Single Credential
requirement.description: Pre-existing installs already store a single most-recent credential. That entry must seed the new list so users don't lose their working host on update.
requirement.rule: On first launch of the new build, if the legacy single-credential Keychain item exists, the app creates one saved entry from it labeled "Last connection" (so the user can rename it later) and removes the legacy item.
Migration runs only when both (a) the legacy item exists and (b) the new saved-connections index is empty for that legacy host. Repeated launches do not create duplicate entries.
After migration completes successfully (or after the user saves any new entry on a fresh install), the legacy single-credential writer is no longer used.
